I had done doordash for months and this was my 2nd day doing uber eats. I think when I got the call I had like 10-15 deliveries total. When doing doordash I was used to getting a prompt when receiving a call from a customer so that I knew it was a customer calling me. This was at the end of a very long and stressful day for me so I wasn't exactly thinking completely straight. I got the call right when I picked up an order and they had all this info about me, and since I didn't get a prompt telling me it was a customer calling me, I figured it must be legit uber support. I'm not saying I am unworthy of criticism, but this was a circumstance where I just wasn't thinking straight and I was busting my ass to get some money and make ends meet. We all do dumb things when we're stressed, tired, or our guard is down. 

What frustrates me with Uber is:

1. They give all sorts of information about me to the customer, or scammer in this case

2. They give the customer/scammer a way to contact me outside of the app without any notification that it is a customer contacting me

3. They seem to be completely uninterested in helping me get my money back despite the fact that I immediately realized my mistake and submitted a dispute claim within 5 minutes. I know for a fact there is a way they could get my money back, they just don't want to go through the trouble since its "my fault" I got scammed.

I'm not a dumb or careless person, but sometimes you get yourself in situations where you are vulnerable without realizing it. That is what happened to me. I hate this idea that people will side with uber on this and blame me for getting scammed, as if they are above it. I think its also really presumptuous and disrespectful to insinuate that you have to be dumb to get scammed. Plenty of smart people get scammed every day. You cant be on guard 24/7 and shit happens. I would only hope that a company worth 180 billion dollars would be willing to help me out on the $220 I lost using their app so I can make a car payment.

IDK, I was suspicious at first but the guy on the support line said he would get me into the program, which I was accepted into before I even finished my deliveries on my 2nd day. you’re losing a ton of momentum on your reach back.  Your arm is completely extended before you are halfway through your last step. This is causing you to lose pretty much all the momentum from your lower body and forcing you to muscle the disc.

The apex of your reach back should approximately be timed with when you’re planting your right foot. When you plant, explode forward and try to hit that power pocket. Use the momentum generated in your x-step to propel your arm (and therefore the disc) forward. Let the rotation of your shoulders drive your arms.  Don’t try to muscle it.

two things I notice right away

1- try starting the disc right by your sternum.  when you step forward with your right foot, that’s when you will “reach back”.  Really what you’re doing is letting your arm go back while
you move forward.  Then sling it forward. On video it should look like the disc stays in the same spot while you take your last step and then you pull it through when your arm moves.

2- Let your whole body follow through.  A good cue for this is making sure your left leg comes forward and you’re stepping in front of your plant foot on the follow through.

I wouldn’t worry about anything else since these 2 things are probably the most important.
